# State Store & Synthetic Data

Mock data should read like the real site, and state should survive a reload. The shape of the data comes from `spec.data`, which is inferred from real samples. Starter schemas for each site type are in [archetypes/](archetypes/).

---

## 1. Store (`js/store.js`, generated by scaffold)

`scaffold_replica.js` generates the store from `spec.state` (`initial`, `persist`), `spec.locale`, `spec.currency` and `spec.currencyDigits`. Nobody edits it during the build. One store is shared by every view and by `shell.js`. `app.js` subscribes and re-renders the active view and the shell on every change, so views don't subscribe themselves. Only the `persist` keys go to `localStorage`, read with a guard: bad JSON or a value of the wrong type falls back to `initial`.

```javascript
import { store, addItem, setItemQty, removeItem, countItems, sumItems, money } from '../store.js';

store.get().cart;                                               // read
store.set(s => ({ cart: addItem(s.cart, id) }));                // add 1 (or addItem(list, id, qty))
store.set(s => ({ cart: setItemQty(s.cart, id, 3) }));          // qty ≤ 0 removes
store.set(s => ({ cart: removeItem(s.cart, id) }));
countItems(store.get().cart);                                   // badge count
money(sumItems(store.get().cart, id => byId[id].price));        // subtotal, formatted for spec.locale / currency
```

Cart-like lists are arrays of `{ id, qty }`, so write them that way in `spec.state.initial`. A new piece of state (a filter, a dismissed banner) goes in the spec: the orchestrator adds it to `spec.state`, then regenerates just the store with `rm <replica>/js/store.js && node <skill>/scripts/scaffold_replica.js --dir <replica>`. The full generated API (router `href`, ui helpers) is in [spec-schema.md](spec-schema.md#what-scaffold-generates).

Put actions (`addToCart`, `toggleFilter`, …) in the view or `shell.js` that owns the feature, written with these helpers.

---

## 2. Data that reads like the real site

`js/data.js` exists from minute 0: scaffold writes it from `spec.data.seed` (at most 6 records: every fixture a feature step needs plus 1–2 more) and `spec.data.extras`, so Builders develop against real-looking data at once. The Data agent ([agents/data.md](agents/data.md)) then swaps in the full set, same shape, keeping every seed record. The Analyst writes the seed and the Data agent the full set by the same rules:

1. **Start from the samples.** `capture.json → pages[].cardGroups[].samples` holds real item text. Note the patterns in it:
   - how titles are built (brand + model + variant? truncated with "…"?) and how long they are;
   - the price format (`£51.77`, `$1,299.00`, `₹2,499`) and the price range;
   - the rating scale and precision (5 stars, or 4.6 out of 5), and the review-count range;
   - badge wording and how often badges appear;
   - stock and delivery phrasing ("In stock", "Only 3 left", "FREE delivery Tue, 30 Sep").
2. **Match the distribution.** Real catalogues are skewed: most prices are mid-range, a few are high; most ratings are 4.0–4.7; badges appear on a minority of items. Avoid uniform or round numbers (`10.00`, `20.00`) unless the samples use them.
3. **Be deterministic.** Use literal records, or a seeded generator so every load gives the same data:
   ```javascript
   const rand = (s => () => (s = (s + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0, s = Math.imul(s ^ (s >>> 15), 1 | s), s ^= s + Math.imul(s ^ (s >>> 7), 61 | s), ((s ^ (s >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296))(42);
   const pick = arr => arr[Math.floor(rand() * arr.length)];
   ```
4. **Keep fields consistent with each other.** Write these as `spec.data.rules` so that `check_replica.js` enforces them:

   | Rule | Expression |
   |---|---|
   | Discount only when there's a list price | `r.listPrice == null \|\| r.listPrice > r.price` |
   | "Only N left" matches stock | `r.stock > 5 \|\| /only/i.test(r.stockText)` |
   | Review count covers the listed reviews | `!r.reviews \|\| r.reviewCount >= r.reviews.length` |
   | Rating agrees with the reviews listed | `!r.reviews?.length \|\| Math.abs(r.rating - avg(r.reviews)) < 0.6` (define `avg` inline) |
   | Dates are in the right order | `new Date(r.checkIn) < new Date(r.checkOut)` |

5. **Match locale and currency.** Use `spec.locale`, `spec.currency` and `spec.currencyDigits`. Views format prices with `money(n)` from `store.js` or `priceHtml(n)` from `ui.js`, both built on the same `MONEY_OPTIONS`, so never format a price by hand. Use names and places from that locale.
6. **Match images to items.** Each record's image is `assets/img/<key>.jpg`, and `assets/images.manifest.json` maps the key to a keyword built from the record. [media-and-asset-pipeline.md](media-and-asset-pipeline.md) has the download step.
7. **Plain module.** `js/data.js` must not touch `window` or `document` when it is imported, because the checker imports it in Node.

---

## 3. Search, filter and sort (a pattern for views)

```javascript
export function query(items, { text = '', filters = {}, sort }) {
  const q = text.trim().toLowerCase();
  const out = items.filter(it =>
    (!q || [it.title, it.brand, it.category].some(v => v?.toLowerCase().includes(q))) &&
    Object.entries(filters).every(([k, v]) =>
      v == null || v === '' || (Array.isArray(v) ? !v.length || v.includes(it[k]) : typeof v === 'object' ? it[k] >= (v.min ?? -Infinity) && it[k] <= (v.max ?? Infinity) : it[k] === v)));
  const [key, dir] = (sort || '').split(':');
  return key ? out.sort((a, b) => (a[key] > b[key] ? 1 : -1) * (dir === 'desc' ? -1 : 1)) : out;
}
```

Debounce text input by about 150 ms. Show the result count and an empty state, and make sure both have `data-testid`s so features can check them.
